gaps.description: While general e-wallet adoption in Malaysian urban centers has been extensively modeled via UTAUT2 (P1), existing empirical frameworks fail to account for specific micro-merchant cybersecurity trust deficits and QR tampering vulnerabilities in semi-rural commercial corridors (P2, P4).

Although national fintech digitization policies subsidize merchant acquisition (P1, P3), the dual barrier of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) transaction fees and digital financial illiteracy among traditional family-run grocers in East Malaysia remains unaddressed in standard technology acceptance literature (P3, P5).

Current literature investigates post-pandemic operational transitions for urban F&B micro-enterprises (P6) and Shariah compliance perception in digital wallets (P7), yet there is a critical gap evaluating how BNM regulatory compliance requirements (P9) constrain Islamic fintech feature innovation for rural micro-retailers.
